content: Handyman bash scripts most often fail destructively: deleting files without a dry-run/preview, building rm paths from unvalidated/empty variables (rm -rf ${p}/* becomes rm -rf /), using find|xargs rm without -print0/-0, no set -euo pipefail so partial failures are silent, and no trap for temp cleanup. Safer patterns: prefix-guard destructive targets, default to dry-run, quote everything, use find -delete or xargs -0, and add shellcheck + bats tests.
